about: The prayer Leo XIII composed for the prayers said after low Mass, where it stands after the collect. It asks Saint Michael the Archangel to defend us in battle against the wickedness and snares of the devil. It then prays that God may rebuke the devil, and again addresses Saint Michael, as prince of the heavenly host, asking him by the power of God to cast Satan and the other evil spirits into hell.

s01.translation: Saint Michael the Archangel, defend us in battle. Be our protection against the wickedness and snares of the devil.

s02.translation: May God rebuke him, we humbly pray.

s03.translation: And do thou, O Prince of the heavenly hosts, by the power of God, thrust into hell Satan, and all the evil spirits, who prowl about the world seeking the ruin of souls. Amen.

w013.function: Future imperative of “sum”. The present imperative is “es”.

w015.function: A subjunctive of wish. Its subject is “Deus” (w017), and the verb governs the dative “illi” (w016).

w018.function: Nominative plural adjective referring to the understood subject of “deprecámur” (w019).

w019.function: A deponent: passive in form, active in meaning.

w020.function: Explicit subject pronoun. The enclitic “-que” joins this clause to the preceding one.

w025.function: Accusative plural agreeing with “spíritus” (w026). The enclitic “-que” joins it to “sátanam” (w024).

w032.function: A deponent compound of per and vagor, meaning “to roam through”.
